function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

### The best city in Iceland for an ice‑hockey fan: **Reykjavík**

| Why Reykjavík stands out | Details |
|---------------------------|---------|
| **Home of the national team** | The Icelandic national team (the “Icelandic Penguins”) plays its home games at the **Laugardalur Ice Hall** in Reykjavík. It’s the only arena in the country that hosts international fixtures. |
| **Largest ice‑hockey arena** | Laugardalur Ice Hall has a seating capacity of ~1,200 and offers modern facilities, a full‑size rink, and a dedicated training area. |
| **Regular league action** | The **Icelandic Hockey League (Íshokkísamband Íslands)**’s top division games are played here. You’ll see the best local talent, including players who have gone on to play in Sweden, Finland, and the NHL. |
| **Ice‑hockey culture** | Reykjavík hosts the annual **Icelandic Ice Hockey Festival** (usually in February), featuring exhibition matches, youth clinics, and a “Hockey Night” event with live music and food. |
| **Convenient travel hub** | As the capital, Reykjavík has the most frequent flights (both domestic and international), a well‑connected bus network, and plenty of accommodation options ranging from budget hostels to luxury hotels. |
| **Other attractions** | While you’re there, you can combine your hockey trip with Iceland’s iconic sights: the Blue Lagoon, Golden Circle, Hallgrímskirkja church, and the vibrant nightlife of Laugavegur. |

---

#### Quick itinerary for a 3‑day hockey trip

| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
|-----|---------|-----------|---------|
| **1** | Arrive in Reykjavík, check into hotel | Explore Laugardalur Ice Hall (tour, meet the staff) | Dinner at **Matur og Drykkur** (traditional Icelandic cuisine) |
| **2** | Attend a practice session (if open to visitors) | Watch a league match (check the schedule) | Attend the **Icelandic Ice Hockey Festival** event |
| **3** | Visit the **National Museum of Iceland** or **Harpa Concert Hall** | Take a short day trip to the **Blue Lagoon** | Fly home or stay another night for a relaxed departure |

---

#### Alternative options (if you want a smaller town vibe)

| City | Highlights |
|------|------------|
| **Akureyri** | Second‑largest city, hosts the **Akureyri Ice Hall** (smaller but cozy). Good for a quieter stay and scenic fjord views. |
| **Kópavogur** | Near Reykjavík, has a community rink and is a good base if you want to avoid the capital’s crowds. |

---

### Bottom line

If you’re looking for the **most comprehensive ice‑hockey experience**—from watching top‑level games to immersing yourself in Iceland’s hockey culture—**Reykjavík** is the clear winner. Its world‑class arena, national team presence, and easy accessibility make it the ideal destination for any hockey enthusiast visiting Iceland.
